## Food-Point System — Developer Build Specification (Version 1)

**Product:** Code Hustlers — Food-Point Billing & POS (offline desktop application)
**Audience:** Developers + Claude Code
**Status:** Locked for Version 1 build
**Owner:** Abdul Moiz (Founder). All license keys are generated by the founder's office only.

> **How to read this document.** This is the **third** product in the Code Hustlers offline-desktop line, after Shop Inventory and Pharmacy. It is built **on top of** the same foundation — same architecture, licensing, backup, offline rules, and design discipline. To avoid repeating everything, this spec is organised as:
> - **REUSED AS-IS** — take it directly from the shop spec and the shop repo (`../POS-Shop-Inventory-System/`). Do not redesign it.
> - **CHANGED** — same idea as the shop, but the food-point needs a different version.
> - **NEW** — food-only, does not exist in the shop or pharmacy apps.
>
> Claude Code: read the shop spec (and reuse the shop repo code) first, then apply the deltas below. This is a **new repository** (`codehustlers-food`); do not modify the shop or pharmacy repos.

> **One honest scope note up front.** "Food-point" covers a range: a takeaway/counter fast-food point, a small café, a dhaba, or a small dine-in restaurant. This spec covers **all of them** by making **dine-in tables** and **kitchen tickets** *toggleable* in Settings. A pure takeaway counter turns tables off and bills in seconds; a small restaurant turns them on. Build both; let Settings decide which a given customer sees.

## 1. What we are building (read this first)

A **fully offline** billing and order-management app for small food businesses — takeaway counters, cafés, dhabas, and small dine-in restaurants — installed on the business's own Windows computer and shipped as a single `.exe`.

We do **not** win on price. We win on the same offline promise as the other two products, plus what a food point actually needs every day:

> **Take an order in seconds, get it to the kitchen without confusion, settle the bill fast, and at night know exactly how much you really made.**

The shop app's hooks were expiry alerts and daily profit. A food point doesn't care about expiry. Its two hooks are different:

1. **A fast, forgiving order flow that just works offline** — tap items on a grid, fire them to the kitchen, hold several tables at once, settle in one tap. Many cheap billing tools are clumsy at exactly this. We are not.
2. **Knowing the real numbers** — daily profit, best-selling items, and busiest hours. Small food owners rarely know these. Showing them plainly is a genuine reason to buy.

### The single job of the app
> A cashier opens it, takes orders all day (at the counter or across tables), sends each order to the kitchen, settles bills fast, and the owner sees at night how much they sold, how much profit they made, and what sold best.

---

## 2. Non-negotiable principles

Same discipline as the other two. Decided — do not re-open during the build.

| # | Principle | Why |
|---|-----------|-----|
| 1 | **100% offline.** No feature may require internet to function. | Core promise and market strength. |
| 2 | **Local data only.** All data lives in a local SQLite database on the machine. | Offline. No cloud in v1. |
| 3 | **Order-taking speed beats everything.** Minimum taps from "new order" to "sent to kitchen" to "paid". | This is a high-pressure, repeated-all-day workflow. Speed *is* the product. |
| 4 | **Prints to thermal printers (ESC/POS)** — a customer bill, and a kitchen ticket. | Decided. Works with no internet. |
| 5 | **Node-locked licensing**, founder-issued. The software never generates its own key. | Anti-copy. Identical to the other products. |
| 6 | **One-click backup** to USB or folder, no internet. | Sales data = our reputation. |
| 7 | **Beautiful, fast, touch-first UI.** Food POS is used on touchscreens under pressure. | Clarity and speed are the design. |
| 8 | **Frontend in Next.js**, packaged as a Windows `.exe`. | Team standard. |

### Out of scope for Version 1 (do NOT build yet)
- Cloud sync, online accounts, or any server.
- Online-ordering / aggregator integration (Foodpanda, etc.), delivery-rider tracking, customer-facing apps. *(All need internet — against principle #1.)*
- **Full ingredient-level inventory and recipe costing.** v1 uses a **simple estimated food cost per menu item** for profit. Recipes that deduct raw ingredients per sale are a big, separate system — **defer** (later, not never), exactly as we deferred drug-interaction checking in the pharmacy.
- Kitchen Display Screen (KDS). The **printed** kitchen ticket is enough for v1; an on-screen kitchen view is a future add.
- Loyalty / CRM / customer accounts, table reservations, staff time-tracking/payroll.
- Multi-branch, multi-currency, tax/GST engines, accounting exports, mobile app.

Keep v1 lean and fast. These are the "later" list.

## 3. Tech stack & architecture

**REUSED AS-IS** from the shop spec. Same Electron + Next.js (static export) + better-sqlite3 + electron-builder, same one-machine no-network architecture, same safe IPC.

**Data location:** `%APPDATA%/CodeHustlersFood/` (its own folder, so all three products can coexist on one machine if ever needed). SQLite file + encrypted license file live here, not in `Program Files`.

> **Do not skip this when forking:** Electron derives `userData` from the app name, so without an override the folder becomes `%APPDATA%/Code Hustlers Food Point/` and the path above is silently wrong. Call `app.setName('CodeHustlersFood')` **before** `app.whenReady()` in `electron/main.ts`, exactly as the pharmacy does (`app.setName('CodeHustlersPharmacy')`).

Everything the three `offline-desktop-*` skills encode (safe IPC, no raw SQL to the renderer, WAL mode, verify-only licensing, backup/restore, ESC/POS printing) applies unchanged.

---

## 4. Data model (SQLite schema)

The shop had `items` and a one-shot `invoices`. The food-point replaces both: a **menu** (catalogue) and **orders that stay open** and become the bill when settled. There is no separate `invoices` table — **a settled order is the invoice.**

### NEW / CHANGED tables

**menu_categories** *(NEW)*
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | INTEGER PK | |
| name | TEXT | e.g. "Fast Food", "BBQ", "Drinks", "Deals" |
| sort_order | INTEGER | controls grid order |

**menu_items** *(CHANGED from `items` — no expiry, no batch, no stock)*
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | INTEGER PK | |
| name | TEXT | required — e.g. "Chicken Biryani" |
| category_id | INTEGER FK | |
| sale_price | REAL | menu price |
| cost_price | REAL | **estimated food cost — needed for profit.** An estimate is fine in v1. |
| is_available | INTEGER (0/1) | quick "86 this item" toggle when the kitchen runs out |
| barcode | TEXT | nullable (rare in food, but harmless) |
| sort_order | INTEGER | |
| notes | TEXT | nullable (kitchen note default) |

**modifier_groups** *(NEW — optional but very useful for food)*
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | INTEGER PK | |
| name | TEXT | e.g. "Size", "Spice level", "Add-ons" |
| selection_type | TEXT | `single` or `multi` |

**modifiers** *(NEW)*
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | INTEGER PK | |
| group_id | INTEGER FK | |
| name | TEXT | e.g. "Large", "Extra cheese", "No onions" |
| price_delta | REAL | +/- amount added to the line (0 for "No onions") |

**item_modifier_groups** *(NEW — which groups apply to which menu item)*
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| item_id | INTEGER FK | part of the composite primary key |
| group_id | INTEGER FK | part of the composite primary key |

> Modifiers can start simple: if the team wants to ship faster, v1 may launch with **free-text line notes only** (e.g. "less spicy") and add structured modifier groups next. Build the tables now; wiring the full UI is the extensible part.

**tables** *(NEW — dine-in only; ignored when tables are toggled off)*
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | INTEGER PK | |
| name | TEXT | "T1", "Garden 3", etc. |
| area | TEXT | nullable — "Indoor", "Rooftop" |
| seats | INTEGER | nullable |

> **Table status is derived, never stored.** A table is `occupied` iff an `open` order references it — read it with a `LEFT JOIN orders ON orders.table_id = tables.id AND orders.status = 'open'`, which returns the running total in the same query. Storing a `status` column creates a second source of truth: any crash between "settle" and "free the table" strands the table as permanently occupied with no way back. A floor is a handful of rows; the join is free.

**orders** *(CHANGED — this is the heart; replaces one-shot `invoices`)*
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | INTEGER PK | |
| order_no | TEXT | human-readable, sequential per day — see the numbering rule below. `UNIQUE` |
| type | TEXT | `dine_in` / `takeaway` / `delivery` |
| table_id | INTEGER FK | nullable (dine-in only) |
| status | TEXT | `open` / `settled` / `void` |
| opened_at | TEXT (ISO) | |
| settled_at | TEXT (ISO) | nullable until paid |
| customer_name | TEXT | nullable |
| customer_phone | TEXT | nullable (useful for delivery/takeaway call-outs) |
| subtotal | REAL | |
| discount | REAL | default 0 |
| service_charge | REAL | default 0 (optional %, from settings) |
| total | REAL | |
| profit | REAL | computed & stored **at settle time** from snapshots |
| payment_method | TEXT | nullable (cash/card) |
| void_reason | TEXT | nullable — required when `status = 'void'` |
| voided_at | TEXT (ISO) | nullable |

> **Order numbering.** `order_no` is `YYYYMMDD-NNN` (e.g. `20260811-014`), where `NNN` restarts at 001 each business day. It is assigned **inside the `openOrder` transaction**, taking the largest suffix already issued under today's prefix and adding one (`SELECT MAX(order_no) FROM orders WHERE order_no LIKE '20260811-%'`, then parse and increment) — never precomputed in the UI, and never `COUNT(*)`, which reuses a number as soon as an order is voided. With several orders opened in quick succession, anything outside the transaction collides. The `UNIQUE` constraint is the backstop that turns a numbering bug into an error instead of two orders sharing a number.

**order_items** *(CHANGED — snapshot everything; track kitchen state)*
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | INTEGER PK | |
| order_id | INTEGER FK | |
| menu_item_id | INTEGER FK | |
| item_name | TEXT | snapshot at add time |
| qty | REAL | |
| cost_price | REAL | snapshot — for accurate historical profit |
| sale_price | REAL | snapshot |
| line_total | REAL | includes modifier deltas |
| notes | TEXT | nullable (e.g. "no onions") |
| kitchen_status | TEXT | `new` / `fired` / `served` / `void` |
| fired_at | TEXT (ISO) | when it was sent to the kitchen (drives the KOT) |
| void_reason | TEXT | nullable — required when `kitchen_status = 'void'` |
| voided_at | TEXT (ISO) | nullable |

**order_item_modifiers** *(NEW — snapshot chosen modifiers per line)*
| Column | Type | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| id | INTEGER PK | |
| order_item_id | INTEGER FK | |
| name | TEXT | snapshot at add time |
| price_delta | REAL | snapshot at add time — already folded into `order_items.line_total` |

**settings** — same key/value store, food additions: `business_name`, `business_address`, `business_phone`, `printer_customer`, `printer_kitchen`, `enable_tables` (0/1), `enable_kitchen_print` (0/1), `service_charge_percent` (default 0), `currency_symbol`, `manager_pin` (see below).

> **The one permission in v1: a manager PIN.** §5.3 calls voids a permissioned action, so v1 needs something to check against — but a full users/roles/login system is out of scope and would slow the counter down. The whole model is a single optional 4-digit `manager_pin` in settings: **if it is set, voiding an item or an order prompts for it; if it is blank, voids are open.** Nothing else in the app is gated. The PIN is stored hashed, verified in the main process (never compared in the renderer), and the void proceeds only on a successful check. Owners who don't want the friction leave it empty.

**license**, **backup_log** — **REUSED AS-IS**.

> **Profit rule (unchanged principle):** profit is computed at **settle time** from the snapshots on `order_items`, never from live menu data. Changing a menu price tomorrow must not change today's recorded profit. Food cost is an estimate — that's acceptable and clearly the owner's number to set.
>
> **The formula, precisely — profit follows the money actually taken:**
>
> ```
> cogs   = Σ (qty × cost_price)              over non-void lines
> profit = total − cogs                      where total = subtotal − discount + service_charge
> ```
>
> Deriving profit from `total` rather than from per-line margins is what keeps it honest, and it fixes two ways the naive `Σ qty × (sale_price − cost_price)` lies:
> - **Paid modifiers.** A "+150 extra cheese" is folded into `line_total` and so into `subtotal`, but it appears in no line's `sale_price`. Per-line margin drops that revenue on the floor.
> - **Discounts.** A discount reduces what the customer paid but touches no line, so per-line margin reports profit the business never made. Same for a service charge in the other direction.
>
> Cost stays per-line because that is the part the snapshots exist to protect.

## 5. Modules

Shared skeleton, food-specific content. **NEW** modules marked.

### 5.1 Dashboard — CHANGED
The owner's/cashier's morning glance:
- **Today's sales** and **Today's profit** (big, green).
- **Open orders** count (and open tables), tappable to resume.
- Today's **order count**, and a small **best-seller today** + **busiest hour** peek.
- Large **New order** button.
- Short list of recent settled orders.
*(No expiry strip — not relevant to food.)*

### 5.2 Menu — CHANGED (was Items)
Manage what's for sale.
- Categories + items with price, **estimated food cost**, availability, sort order.
- **"86 / available" toggle** per item — one tap to mark sold-out so it greys out on the order screen. Cooks run out; this must be instant.
- Attach modifier groups (Size, Spice, Add-ons) to items.
- Fast search; category tabs.

### 5.3 Order taking — CHANGED (was Billing; the core screen)
Speed is everything. Touch-first.
- Start an order and pick **type**: **Dine-in** (choose a table) / **Takeaway** / **Delivery** (optional name/phone).
- **Item grid by category** — tap to add; adjust qty; pick modifiers; add a line note.
- **Send to kitchen** fires the *new, not-yet-fired* items → prints a **kitchen ticket** (§5.5) and marks them `fired`. You can add more items later and fire again (a second ticket with only the new items).
- **Hold** the order open and start/resume others — **many orders open at once** (several tables + takeaways in parallel). This is the biggest behavioural difference from the shop's one-shot sale.
- **Settle:** show the bill, apply discount / optional service charge, take payment method, **print customer bill**, mark `settled`, free the table.
- **Void** an item or a whole order with a reason — the reason is required and stored on the row (`void_reason` + `voided_at`), which is what the voids report reads. Gated by the `manager_pin` when one is set (§4).
- Reprint a bill; resume any open order.

### 5.4 Tables / floor — NEW (dine-in; toggleable)
- A simple grid of tables showing **free / occupied** and the running total on each occupied table.
- Tap a free table → start its order; tap an occupied one → resume.
- Turned off entirely when `enable_tables = 0` (pure takeaway counters never see it).
- Keep it light: no reservations, no floor-plan drag-drop in v1 — just clear, tappable table cards.

### 5.5 Kitchen ticket (KOT) — NEW
- A **second print format** to the kitchen printer, fired from the order screen.
- Prints **only the newly-fired items**, large and legible: order no + type + table, time, each item with qty + modifiers + notes. **No prices** — the kitchen doesn't need money, it needs clarity.
- Works fully offline. If the business has a single printer, `enable_kitchen_print = 0` (or route the ticket to the same printer) — the app must not break on one-printer setups.

### 5.6 Reports — CHANGED
Plain, readable, printable, food-flavoured:
- **Daily & date-range sales and profit** (reused).
- **Sales by order type** (dine-in vs takeaway vs delivery).
- **Best-selling items** (by qty and by revenue) — what to promote, what to drop.
- **Sales by hour** — the busiest-times view that helps staffing.
- **Voids report** — visibility on cancelled items/orders.
- **Daily profit** breakdown.

### 5.7 Daily profit view — *Differentiator* — REUSED AS-IS
Green dashboard card: "Today you sold X and earned Y profit." Profit = sum of stored `orders.profit` for settled orders today.

### 5.8 Backup — REUSED AS-IS
One-click backup/restore to USB/folder, timestamped, `backup_log`, gentle reminder. Never auto-delete data.

### 5.9 Licensing — REUSED AS-IS
Node-locked, founder-issued, verify-only. `product: "food"` in the key payload. Lifetime + time-limited supported.

### 5.10 Settings — CHANGED
Business name/address/phone (printed on the bill), **customer printer** + **kitchen printer** selection, **enable tables** toggle, **enable kitchen print** toggle, optional **service charge %**, optional **manager PIN** (set/change/clear — blank means voids are open), currency symbol, Backup/Restore.

## 6. Design system — colour, type, layout, UX

**Same discipline as the other two** — calm, fast, tabular numbers, big totals, dark sidebar + light workspace, keyboard/touch-first. **Everything is reused EXCEPT the palette**, which is a distinct **warm hospitality** identity so the food product has its own face.

**Why this theme:** shop is cool navy (retail), pharmacy is clinical teal (health). A food point should feel **warm, appetising, and inviting** — so we use a **deep espresso sidebar on a warm-paper workspace, with a confident tomato accent.** The warm background alone makes it feel different from the cool backgrounds of the other two the moment it opens.

### 6.1 Colour tokens (use these exact values — this is the food palette)

```css
:root {
  /* Brand & structure — warm hospitality */
  --brand-espresso:       #2B211C;  /* side nav, headers — deep warm espresso */
  --brand-espresso-hover: #201813;
  --accent:               #E24B32;  /* primary actions: Send to kitchen, Charge — appetising tomato */
  --accent-hover:         #C43D28;

  /* Surfaces — warm, not cool */
  --bg:                   #FAF7F3;  /* warm-paper workspace */
  --surface:              #FFFFFF;
  --border:               #ECE4DB;

  /* Text */
  --text:                 #241E1B;
  --text-muted:           #6E635C;

  /* Semantic (reserve for meaning, never decoration) */
  --success:              #2E9E5B;  /* profit, paid, positive money */
  --warning:              #E0A400;  /* attention (used lightly — few warnings in food) */
  --danger:               #B02A37;  /* deep crimson — void, delete, unpaid. Deliberately DEEPER than the tomato accent so "void" ≠ "charge". */
}
```

**Semantic discipline (important here):** the **accent tomato** (`--accent`) and the **danger crimson** (`--danger`) are both warm reds, so they are pitched **deliberately apart** — bright tomato = *go* (charge, fire to kitchen), deeper crimson = *undo/stop* (void, delete). Keep that contrast; never blur them. Green = money/paid. Never use semantic colours decoratively.

### 6.2 Typography — REUSED AS-IS
Inter (bundled offline), **tabular numbers** on all prices/totals/quantities, **big totals** (the bill total and today's profit are the largest text on their screens), sentence case, buttons name the action (**Send to kitchen**, **Charge**, **Print bill**). Keep strings in one `strings.ts` for future Urdu.

### 6.3 Layout — CHANGED (food flow)
- **Espresso left sidebar:** Dashboard, New order, Tables, Menu, Reports, Settings. (Tables hidden when toggled off.)
- **Order screen is a two-panel workspace:** a big **item grid** (category tabs across the top) on the left for fast tapping, and the **running order panel** on the right (lines, qty, modifiers, running total, **Send to kitchen** + **Charge**).
- Warm-paper workspace, white cards, **large touch targets** — this is a touchscreen tool used under pressure.

### 6.4 UX principles — REUSED, with food emphasis
- **Order-taking speed beats everything.** The fewest possible taps from item → fire → paid.
- **Sold-out is one tap** and instantly visible (greyed item) on the order grid.
- **Many orders open at once must never get confusing** — clear table/order labels, obvious "which order am I on".
- **Errors are plain:** "This table already has an open order — resume it?" — never a code.
- Touch-first, but keyboard shortcuts for a counter with a keyboard are a nice bonus.
- Respect reduced motion; keep it quick and unfussy.

## 7. Licensing implementation — REUSED AS-IS
Identical to the shop/pharmacy §7. Node-locked, offline, founder-issued, Ed25519, verify-only, private key stays in the office key-generator. Only difference: `product: "food"` in the signed payload so keys aren't cross-usable between products. **Do not rebuild; reuse and extend the founder key-generator's product field.**

## 8. (Reserved — pricing)
Business decision, documented separately. Does not affect the build (licensing already supports lifetime + time-limited).

## 9. Secondary anti-copy hardening — REUSED AS-IS
Data + license in `%APPDATA%/CodeHustlersFood/`, encrypted license file, no plainly-named license file. The real lock is §7.

## 10. Thermal printing — CHANGED (two formats)
Same ESC/POS approach, now **two** receipts:
- **Customer bill:** business name/address/phone, order no + type + table, datetime, line items (name, modifiers, qty, price, line total), subtotal, discount, service charge (if any), **total**, short thank-you.
- **Kitchen ticket (KOT):** newly-fired items only, **large and legible, no prices**, with order no + type + table + time + item qty/modifiers/notes.
Printers are chosen once in Settings (`printer_customer`, `printer_kitchen`). Must work with no internet, and must degrade gracefully to a single printer.

## 11. Packaging & delivery — REUSED / renamed
Windows `.exe` via electron-builder; first launch runs licensing before use; data persists in `%APPDATA%/CodeHustlersFood/` across updates; uninstaller never deletes data/backups. Remember the native-module rebuild step for better-sqlite3 (the packaging skill covers it).

## 12. Definition of done (v1 checklist)
- [ ] New `codehustlers-food` repository, built on the shop foundation; shop & pharmacy repos untouched.
- [ ] Offline install runs with zero internet.
- [ ] Menu: categories + items with price, **food cost**, availability toggle; modifier groups attachable.
- [ ] Order taking: type (dine-in/takeaway/delivery), item grid, qty, modifiers, line notes; fast.
- [ ] **Send to kitchen** fires new items and prints a **kitchen ticket** (new items only, no prices).
- [ ] **Multiple orders open at once**; hold/resume; settle prints the customer bill and records profit.
- [ ] Tables: free/occupied grid with running totals; fully hidden when `enable_tables = 0`.
- [ ] Void item/order with a required reason stored on the row; gated by `manager_pin` when set.
- [ ] Two-printer support (customer + kitchen) that degrades gracefully to one printer.
- [ ] Reports: daily & range sales/profit, by order type, best sellers, sales by hour, voids.
- [ ] Daily profit view on dashboard, computed as `total − Σ(qty × cost_price)` so paid modifiers and discounts land correctly.
- [ ] One-click backup + restore to USB/folder.
- [ ] Node-locked licensing: Machine ID, verifies founder-issued key offline, `product: food`, blocks on invalid/expired, lifetime + time-limited.
- [ ] Founder key-generator stamps the product field.
- [ ] **Warm hospitality** design system applied (espresso sidebar, warm-paper bg, tomato accent, tabular numbers, big totals).
- [ ] Packaged as `.exe` via electron-builder.

*This document is the single source of truth for Food-Point System v1. It extends the shop spec (sibling repo: `../POS-Shop-Inventory-System/Shop inventory system build spec.md`); where this spec is silent, the shop spec governs. With this, the three-product line — Shop, Pharmacy, Food-Point — shares one architecture, one licensing system, and one design discipline, each with its own face.*
